public_rationale: Crunchbase reported on August 29, 2023 that AI-related companies received more than a quarter of U.S. startup investment dollars in its 2023 year-to-date data [e1]. It also reported AI investment trending higher year over year while investment fell across most industries [e1]. This supports both the funding-share claim and “one of the few reliable roads to capital” when understood as comparative aggregate fundraising resilience within that U.S. measurement window [e1].
limitations: The evidence does not establish an updated share through November 20 or for the completed 2023 calendar year [e1].
The U.S. finding does not establish a global share above 25%; Crunchbase reported 18% globally for the first half of 2023 [e2].
Aggregate fundraising does not establish individual startups' chances of securing capital. Global AI deal counts fell 18% quarter over quarter in Q3 2023 [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI has become one of the few reliable roads to capital, with more than a quarter of 2023 VC startup dollars going to AI companies.

statement.excerpt: Artificial intelligence has become one of the few reliable roads to capital in the current economy, with venture capitalists sinking more than a quarter of their startup dollars into AI-related companies in 2023.

from_speaker: one of the few reliable roads to capital
our_interpretation: Because the post appeared during 2023, the observation concerns year-to-date evidence available before publication, not the completed calendar year.
The post links directly to Crunchbase's August 29 report about American startups. I therefore use its U.S. scope and broad AI-related classification.
Reliable roads to capital means comparatively resilient aggregate fundraising, not guaranteed access for individual startups.
Metric scope is null because this is a sector-wide funding-share claim rather than a claim about one company's money.
criteria.support_condition: The linked U.S. funding dataset places AI-related startups above 25% of 2023 year-to-date startup investment and reports greater funding resilience than the broader startup market.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched U.S. year-to-date data place the share at or below 25%, or show that the asserted relative funding resilience did not exist.

evidence.excerpt: More than 1 in 4 dollars invested in American startups this year has gone to an artificial intelligence-related company, Crunchbase data shows.
evidence.locator: Opening paragraph; subsequent section AI gets a bigger piece of a smaller pie
evidence.explanation: Crunchbase directly reports a share above 25% for American startups. Its accompanying analysis reports increasing AI investment amid a broad funding contraction, supporting the relative-resilience reading.

evidence.excerpt: Companies categorized as AI in Crunchbase raised $25 billion in the first half of 2023, representing 18% of global funding.
evidence.explanation: The global first-half share was below 25%. Geography and measurement window differ, so this limits generalization rather than contradicting the linked U.S. result.

evidence.excerpt: AI deals slipped even further, declining by 18% QoQ to 501 — the lowest quarterly level since 2017.​
evidence.locator: Paragraph following Global AI funding reached $8.3B in Q3’23
evidence.explanation: Falling global deal counts caution against reading reliable as easy financing for every AI startup. Deal count is not the claimed U.S. dollar share.
